claim_tested: CheB-dependent modification of chemoreceptors is deamidation of Gln to methyl-accepting Glu
key_finding: Tryptic peptides K1 and R1 of Tsr sequenced; a site in K1 cannot accept methyl groups without the CheB-dependent modification; correlation with tsr gene sequence identifies the modification as Gln to Glu deamidation
context: Escherichia coli Tsr (MCPI) in vivo labelling
confidence_and_limitations: High for the chemistry; site numbering is given relative to peptides rather than as modern residue numbers in the abstract; organism is E. coli not B. subtilis

claim_tested: CheB-dependent modification creates a free carboxylate
key_finding: At least three CheB-dependent modification sites on Trg; pKa of the created group between 2.2 and 5.8
confidence_and_limitations: High; chemical inference rather than site-resolved mass spectrometry

evidence_type: direct assay (in vitro modification of membrane receptor)
claim_tested: CheB acts as deamidase on intact Tar and requires the NWETF docking pentapeptide
key_finding: Truncated Tar lacking the C-terminal pentapeptide is much less efficiently demethylated and deamidated; CheB binds the isolated pentapeptide
context: Escherichia coli Tar in membrane vesicles
confidence_and_limitations: High for E. coli; B. subtilis receptors lack the NWETF/NWESF pentapeptide (verified: McpA ends ...TKRFKIE, McpB ...TKQFKIE, McpC ...IAKFTL), so this docking mechanism does not transfer

claim_tested: CheB deamidase and esterase use one active site
key_finding: Crystal structure of the Salmonella CheB catalytic domain at 1.75 A; single catalytic triad Ser164/His190/Asp286; the enzyme is described as hydrolysing receptor glutamine or methylglutamate side chains
confidence_and_limitations: High; active site assignment described as tentative in 1995 but subsequently standard

claim_tested: B. subtilis McpB carries glutamines at modification positions that must be deamidated before methylation
key_finding: Four McpB sites named Gln371, Gln595, Glu630, Glu637; McpB(E630D,E637D) retaining only the two Gln sites still releases methanol on asparagine addition
context: Bacillus subtilis McpB as sole receptor
confidence_and_limitations: High for the sites being modification sites; the sites were originally assigned by E. coli consensus, and the paper does not identify the deamidating enzyme

claim_tested: CheD not CheB is the receptor deamidase in B. subtilis
key_finding: CheD catalyses amide hydrolysis of specific glutaminyl side chains of McpA and also deamidates McpB and McpC; the authors state the activity had previously been attributed to CheB
confidence_and_limitations: High; direct competing assignment. Conflicts with PMID:22931217 on whether McpB is a CheD substrate

evidence_type: mutant phenotype + in vitro kinase assay + binding
claim_tested: CheD deamidates McpC Q609 and does not deamidate McpB
key_finding: mcpC-Q609E restores chemotaxis in a cheD background; McpC-Q609E activates CheA much better than unmodified McpC; CheD binds McpC-Q609E better; hydroxyl radical footprinting places CheD binding at the modification sites
confidence_and_limitations: High for McpC Q609. The statement that CheD does not deamidate McpB contradicts PMID:12011078 and leaves McpB Q371/Q595 without an assigned enzyme

claim_tested: A B. subtilis CheB catalytic mutant separates esterase from deamidase
key_finding: cheB(S173C) shows no methanol release on asparagine addition or removal even when induced
confidence_and_limitations: High for loss of esterase output; because Ser173 is the single nucleophile this allele cannot separate the two activities, so it is uninformative for deamidation

claim_tested: McpB Gln371 is equivalent to a demonstrated Tar/Tsr deamidation site
key_finding: Joint segment register scan places Tar Q295 at McpB Q371 (margin only 4 BLOSUM units over the next register); single-site window scans place Tar Q309 and Tsr Q311 at McpB Q371 (37 vs 26, 40 vs 28). Both candidate columns are demonstrated deamidation sites, so the assignment survives but is not resolved to a specific column
context: E. coli Tar/Tsr versus B. subtilis McpA/McpB/McpC/TlpA/TlpB/TlpC, anchored on the conserved tip motif G[FLIV][ASG]VVA[DEG]EVR
confidence_and_limitations: Low to moderate. Full-length identity Tar vs McpB is 12.8 percent; heptad repeats create a two-heptad ambiguity; 9-12 percent of residues in these windows are Gln; the method fails its internal negative control by not recovering McpC Q609 on the mapped Tar E491 column

claim_tested: B. subtilis CheB Ser173 corresponds to E. coli CheB Ser164
key_finding: Single GxSxGG nucleophile elbow in each: E. coli G162-A-S164-T-G-G, B. subtilis G171-T-S173-T-G-G
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate to high for the motif correspondence; global alignment alone is not reliable at this identity

evidence_type: mutant phenotype (amidation mimic, kinase assay, capillary affinity)
claim_tested: The McpB adaptation sites form one functional cluster
key_finding: Three closely spaced adaptation sites at Gln371, Glu630 and Glu637; amidation of 371 raises apparent asparagine affinity and CheA activation, amidation of 630 and 637 lowers kinase activation without changing affinity
confidence_and_limitations: High for the functional clustering, which matches the CA-CA distances measured here (371-637 14.7 A, 630-637 10.7 A). Does not identify the enzyme and does not map the sites independently of the E. coli consensus

citation: this work (computational, AlphaFold AF-P02942/P39215/P54576/P39214 and PDB 1QU7)
claim_tested: McpB Gln371 is equivalent to a demonstrated E. coli deamidation site
key_finding: McpB Gln371 maps to Tsr Ser255 inside the HAMP domain, 42 residues from the Gln297 column. The Tsr Q297/E304/Q311/E493/E502 columns map to McpB Leu413/Gln420/Asp427/Gly609/Ser618 (CA deviations 0.39-1.44 A; 214 CA aligned, RMSD 1.64 A)
context: AlphaFold cytoplasmic domains superposed on each other and on 1QU7 chain A, seeded only on the conserved tip motif
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate to high. Self control (AF Tsr onto 1QU7) resolves columns to +/-1 residue; positive controls McpC Gln609 and McpA Glu615 land 3 and 2 residues from the E502 column. Limitation: AlphaFold monomer hairpins, not dimers, and the 23-residue arm-length difference must be absorbed somewhere between HAMP and the tip, so the exact insertion point is not determined

claim_tested: Tip-anchored sequence registers transfer from E. coli to B. subtilis at the methylation helices
key_finding: Hairpin arm is 185 residues in Tsr and 208 in McpA, McpB and McpC (23 residues, about 3.3 heptads longer). Published McpB sites sit 122-187 A from the tip versus 107-155 A for the Tsr sites
context: Tsr P02942 vs McpA P39214, McpB P39215, McpC P54576
confidence_and_limitations: High for the residue counts, which come from UniProt feature annotation and a regex tip anchor. Axial distances depend on the AlphaFold models and on the principal-axis definition
